Here's what I found about replacing `pug-loader` with `@webdiscus/pug-loader`, including notes on filters and Node.js compatibility.

## Why replace `pug-loader`

The original `pugjs/pug-loader` is no longer maintained. In late 2021 the @webdiscus/pug-loader was implemented as a replacement for pug-loader because pug-loader was outdated and had many issues. As of 2025, only this Pug loader is maintained. All other Pug loaders are dead and have not been maintained for a long time.

## Basic replacement in webpack config

The simplest swap in `module.rules` is:

const path = require('path'); module.exports = { ... module: { rules: [ { test: /\.pug$/, loader: '@webdiscus/pug-loader', }, ], }, };

There are three modes available:

- **compile** (default): In webpack config: `{ test: /\.pug$/, loader: '@webdiscus/pug-loader', options: { mode: 'compile' } }` — the default mode `compile` can be omitted. In JavaScript, the result of require() is a template function.
- **render**: Renders Pug template into pure HTML string.
- **html**: This mode will render the Pug to pure HTML and should be used with an additional loader to handle HTML. In webpack config add to module.rules: `{ test: /\.pug$/, use: [ { loader: 'html-loader', options: { esModule: false } }, { loader: '@webdiscus/pug-loader', options: { mode: 'html' } } ] }`.

## Filters (regarding `test.filter.js` / `:filter` usage)

I didn't find a file specifically named `test.filter.js`, but here's the relevant info on filters, which is likely what you're after:

The goal of built-in filters is to use the most useful lightweight filters without installation. The built-in filters are custom filters that are collected in one place. These filters can be simply enabled via an option. The available built-in filters are :escape :code :highlight :markdown with highlighting of code blocks. By default all built-in filters are disabled. Enable only filters used in your Pug templates.

## Node.js version

The search results did not return specific Node.js version requirements (the `engines` field) for `@webdiscus/pug-loader`. To confirm the exact minimum supported Node.js version, I'd recommend checking the `package.json` `engines` field on the [npm page](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@webdiscus/pug-loader) or the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/webdiscus/pug-loader). Would you like me to search specifically for the Node.js version requirement?

## Note on future direction

If you're doing a broader migration, be aware of the project's evolution: the html-bundler-webpack-plugin absorbed all the functionality of the pug-plugin and the @webdiscus/pug-loader. In early 2024, the pug-plugin completely switched to the universal code of html-bundler-webpack-plugin, and starting from version 5.0, the pug-plugin is the html-bundler-webpack-plugin under the hood, pre-configured for Pug templates.
